topic.readerProblem: Work out what Otterly.AI really costs once prompt slots, annual billing and the Gemini, AI Mode and Claude add-ons are counted, and decide whether it is worth paying for.
topic.connection: Supports choosing between a one-time AI visibility audit and a recurring AI-search tracker, which is the buying decision AEOeye's audit sits in front of.

assessment: The page is documentation-based and says so near the top: it uses Otterly's own pricing page, pricing calculator, prompt calculator and help-center articles as checked on 2026-10-03, with no hands-on testing. It replaces the earlier page's error that extra prompts were available on Lite, adds exact annual totals and the real discount range, a worked full-coverage total for each plan, and Otterly's own prompt-counting rules, then takes a position on Lite, Standard and the Claude add-on. It makes no claim about accuracy, output quality or product experience, and it leaves out unverifiable review-site ratings and quotes that the merged pages carried.

sources.supports: Lite $29 / Standard $189 / Premium $489 monthly with 15 / 100 / 400 prompts, the same four base engines, annual toggle ($25 / $160 / $422 per month), plan feature differences, add-on prices per tier, extra 100 prompts $99 on Standard and Premium and 'not available' on Lite, Enterprise from 1,000 prompts, USD excluding tax.
Three plans plus Enterprise, add-ons available on all plans, packs of 100 on Standard and Premium, prices shown in USD or EUR depending on location.

Annual totals ($300 / $1,920 / $5,064), annual add-on prices, Standard ladder 100/200/300 prompts at $189/$288/$387, Premium ladder 400 to 1,000 prompts at $489 to $1,083, and add-on prices keyed to plan tier rather than prompt count.
Otterly's prompt calculator multiplies countries, languages, categories and prompts per category, with 50 prompts for a basic check and 100 for extensive monitoring.
Prompt slots are per country; one prompt feeding several brand reports counts once; 100-prompt packs only on Standard and Premium.
7-day free trial, no credit card, 50 search prompts and the other trial limits.
Google AI Mode, Gemini and Claude are add-ons available on all plans, Gemini means gemini.google.com, add-ons can be removed in billing.
Prompts run daily across the engines, no manual run and no frequency change, and Otterly's statement that AI responses are not deterministic.
Engines are read through public web interfaces, Otterly says API data can differ from what users see, and Claude is the one engine tracked via API.
Access continues to the end of the billing cycle; tracked data and historical data are deleted after cancellation.
'70+ countries' (updated September 24, 2026) and the four unsupported country/engine pairs named in the page.
Google says AI Mode and AI Overviews may use different models and techniques, so their responses and links differ.
Accuracy varied by up to 15% across runs of LLMs configured to be deterministic (Atil et al., arXiv 2408.04667).

pricing.region: US / USD public prices, excluding tax (Otterly says the help center may show EUR depending on location)
pricing.billing: Monthly prices published; annual billing advertised at 15% off, with published annual totals of $300 (Lite), $1,920 (Standard) and $5,064 (Premium). Enterprise is custom.
pricing.verification: Opened the pricing page, Otterly's pricing calculator, prompt calculator and the help-center pricing, trial, add-on, prompt and cancellation articles on 2026-10-03; recomputed annual savings, full-coverage totals and per-prompt prices from the published inputs and kept the vendor's own inconsistencies visible in the page.
